title: Blue and Shiny: Complete?
objective: Tell whether groups of words like 'blue and shiny' express a complete idea.
introduction: Hi Maxine! 🧩 Milo found the words 'blue and shiny'. Is that a whole sentence? Let's find out what makes an idea complete!

items.prompt: Which group of words is a complete sentence?
items.explanation: “The bird sings” tells who (the bird) and what it does (sings), so it is a complete sentence.

items.prompt: Which group of words is NOT a complete sentence?
items.explanation: “Under the table” names a place but no doer or action, so it is not a complete sentence.

items.prompt: What is missing from 'blue and shiny'?

options.text: who or what is doing the action

items.explanation: “Blue and shiny” only describes, so it is missing who or what is doing the action.

items.prompt: Which group of words tells a complete idea?
items.explanation: “We” is who, and “walk home” is what they do — that is a complete idea.
“Milo” is who, and “drinks milk” is what he does — a complete sentence.
